analyzed_vuln.description: `get_coffset()` calls `blosc_getitem(coffsets, nchunk, 1, &offset)` on the offsets chunk returned by `get_coffsets()` without validating that this buffer is a well-formed Blosc chunk (or even large enough for header fields). In this PoV, malformed frame data makes `coffsets` invalid/truncated, so `blosc_getitem` enters `_blosc_getitem` and reads block-start metadata via `sw32_(bstarts + j)`, causing an out-of-bounds read/SEGV in `sw32_` (blosc-private.h:44).
analyzed_vuln.conditions: The fuzzer passes attacker-controlled bytes to `blosc2_schunk_open_sframe()`, then `blosc2_schunk_decompress_chunk()` triggers `frame_decompress_chunk()` -> `frame_get_lazychunk()` -> `get_coffset()`. If the crafted frame header/coffsets metadata causes `get_coffsets()` to return a pointer to malformed or undersized offsets data, `get_coffset()` still treats it as a valid compressed chunk and invokes `blosc_getitem` with implicit `INT32_MAX` srcsize assumptions, leading to OOB reads during chunk parsing and crash.
